image_description: A close-up photograph of a bright orange coral fungus (Ramaria species) growing on a forest floor covered in pine needles and moss. The fungus features a complex, multi-branched structure arising from a central base, with numerous upright, cylindrical branches that taper towards rounded tips. The color is a vivid, uniform orange-yellow. The background consists of out-of-focus brown pine needles and green moss patches.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific taxonomic classification of the fungus as a coral fungus (Ramaria/Clavulina) and rule out look-alikes or AI hallucinations of generic plant structures.

To verify the structural integrity of the intricate branching. AI often fails to maintain continuous connectivity in complex, thin structures like coral fungi, leading to floating tips or fused branches.
To assess the naturalness of the texture and lighting, checking for subtle AI artifacts like overly smooth surfaces or inconsistent depth of field blur around the complex edges.
To ensure the fungus sits correctly on the ground plane and that the inter-branch spacing has valid 3D depth, avoiding 'flat' or 'pasted-on' appearances.

focus_areas: Connectivity of branch tips (no floating parts)
Boundary sharpness against the busy background (pine needles)
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the tips of the branches. In AI-generated coral fungi, tips often dissolve into the background or merge incorrectly. Verify if the topology auditor finds any broken connections. Also, check if the fine-grained classifier identifies any non-fungal elements mistakenly incorporated into the structure.
